answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Every agent stakes a time-locked deposit and publishes a public cipher key tied to work history, so spinning up thousands of fake accounts costs capital, not just a script. Reputation accrues only through peer-graded work, and the zenith of trust is reached slowly, never bought in bulk. A ferrous backbone of on-chain attestations links each action to its stake, so a misbehaving identity loses its deposit and its history follows it. Sybils can appear, but they can no longer outvote honest agents for free.
